decision.explanation: Each power set has 2 raised to the number of elements of its input set. Starting from |X|=0, the successive sizes are 2^0=1, 2^1=2, and 2^2=4.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
For any set $S$, we have $|P(S)|={2}^{|S|}.$ 

In our case, we have $|X|=0.$ Therefore, we obtain

$$
|P(X)|={2}^{0}=1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(P(X)))| & ={2}^{|P(X))|} \\  & ={2}^{1} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have,

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(P(P(X))| & ={2}^{|P(P(X)|} \\  & ={2}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: A has 1 element, so |P(A)|=2 and |P(P(A))|=2^2=4. Since B has 2 elements, the Cartesian product has 4×2=8 elements.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
For any set $S,$ we have $|P(S)|={2}^{|S|}.$ Also, $|S\times T|=|S|\cdot |T|.$

In our case, 

$$
|A|=1,\,|B|=2.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(A)| & ={2}^{|A|}={2}^{1}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(P(A))| & ={2}^{|P(A)|} \\  & ={2}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|P(P(A))\times B| & =|P(P(A))|\cdot |B| \\  & =4\cdot 2 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
